label: early original-phase w (or u/v following u/v/w)
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t <= 3) & isin(in_tok, [tok("w"), tok("u"), tok("v")]) & ((in_tok == tok("w")) | isin(prev_tok, [tok("w"), tok("u"), tok("v")]))
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase (99.6% of mass), on input tokens w (68% of mass, 22x lift), u (24%) and v (7%); weak on d and n, never on other letters or digits, and essentially never at the delimiter or in the copy phase. Strongest at early positions (t=0..3, about 93% of mass) and fades by t=5. Magnitude goes up when w/u/v come right after other w/u/v tokens: the top examples are runs like v w, w v w, w w w, where the second or third w reaches the max. A u or v on its own (prev token not in {u,v,w}) usually stays below threshold. The predicate (t<=3, in_tok w, or u/v/w right after u/v/w) gets dev F1 0.68 with mass recall 0.81. Precision is limited because w at t<=3 often still stays inactive, so the gating looks graded rather than all-or-none.
